text:
maya: heads up — eu-west prune wave is stuck and it's blocking the GPU pool rollouts. App-of-apps is in PruneInProgress and not finishing :thinking_face:
liam: oncall? i'm looking at the argocd controller logs now, can you paste the root app status?
maya: copied from the console:
```
Name: infra/apps
Namespace: argocd
Health: Degraded
Status: OutOfSync (PruneInProgress)
SyncWave: 4
PruneWave: 2/5 waiting on 12 child apps\```
nate: i can see increased RTT between eu-west controllers and us-east cluster proxies ~700-900ms intermittently. suspect a transient network partition between controller replicas.
liam: that would explain leader churn. argocd-controller logs show repeated lease renew failures: 
```
E0323 10:20:11.123 controller.go:254] failed to renew lease: rpc error: code = DeadlineExceeded desc = context deadline exceeded
E0323 10:20:12.456 controller.go:254] acquired lease, processing prune wave
E0323 10:20:13.789 controller.go:254] lost lease while pruning, aborting
```
maya: infra-bot just alerted on slow RPCs earlier: "argocd-controller-eu-west latency > 500ms"
infra-bot: ALERT: argocd-controller latency spike detected in eu-west-1 at 2026-03-23T10:18:00Z. PagerDuty routed to #eng-infra.
liam: quick triage — pruning is single-leader work. if leader keeps flipping, prune wave can get starved because each leader restart resets prune progress and children remain 'pending prune'.
sre-oncall: options: 1) increase prune.parallelism in argocd-cm to allow more concurrent prunes (temporary), 2) force a single controller leader by scaling to 1 pod in eu-west until network stabilizes, 3) manually resume child apps after killing the flapping pod.
nate: i'm getting a kube view from eu-west - argocd controller pods show OOM restarts and network timeouts.
```
kubectl get pods -n argocd -o wide
NAME                                READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE   IP            NODE
argocd-controller-5f8b7c6d7f-2xk9l 0/1     Running   5          3d    10.240.1.12   ip-10-240-1-34.eu-west-1
argocd-controller-5f8b7c6d7f-7qz2p 1/1     Running   0          3d    10.240.2.55   ip-10-240-2-99.eu-west-1
```
liam: i'm going to cordon and drain the node with the flapping controller pod, then recreate the controller to force a clean leader election. doing a quick kube-ops rollback of the controller deployment to restart the pod gracefully.
maya: FYI this is blocking the gpu-autoscaler Helm release in the app-of-apps tree; several gpu pools stayed at 0 and workloads are queuing. cost/latency impact noted in console.
liam: rolled the controller pod and bumped argocd-cm prune.parallelism=8 as a temporary mitigation. also decreased argocd-controller replicas to 1 for eu-west via the placement constraint so leader stays stable while we investigate network.
argo-bot: argocd app sync infra/apps triggered by liam (manual sync). Sync operation id: sync-0a9f.
sre-oncall: after the restart, prune wave progressed. i'll keep monitoring for 30 minutes, please verify GPU pools are scaling back up.
maya: seeing child apps move to Synced and prune counts drop. autoscaler started provisioning nodes for gpu-pool-usw2-eu-west overlay. :thumbsup:
liam: leaving a follow-up ticket to address root cause (cross-region VPN routing + MTU + kube-proxy conn tracking). suggest adding health-checks to detect argocd RPC latency and auto-failover policy rather than scale-to-1 hack.
nate: logging saved to s3 at s3://redwood-incidents/2026-03-23/argocd-eu-west-prune-latency.log
sre-oncall: incident notes: cause - transient network partition + controller leader churn; mitigation - restart controller, temporary prune.parallelism increase, restrict leader election to a stable node; impact - 12 child apps pruned slowly, gpu pool rollout delayed ~18 minutes; next steps - routing team to debug VPN MTU and conntrack, infra to add argocd latency alert thresholds.
maya: thanks team — closed the immediate blocker, moving to postmortem channel for RCA. :sparkles:
